domain: Reads 16 consecutive field-map cells (u32 each) from the toroidal 128x128 cell array at 0x02010000 -- one fixed metatile row, walking columns -- and for each cell's low 12 bits (its metatile id, extracted with a shift-fusion '(cell<<20)>>17' that doubles as a *8 byte-stride multiply) copies an 8-byte metatile definition entry from 0x02020000/0x02020004 (top-row tile pair, bottom-row tile pair) as two raw 32-bit stores into a caller-selected VRAM screenblock (0x06002800 + a0<<11), 64 bytes (one tilemap row) apart. Confirmed independently via m2c against real project types: m2c's raw decompilation reads from 0x02010000 and writes from 0x02020000/0x02020004 in the same roles derived here by hand, from directly recomputed PC-relative literal-pool addresses in the retained assembly.
notes: The generated family report's best guess (below the 7500/10000 adoption threshold, at 7436) was games/gs1/src/ui/window/clear_tile_attributes_in_rect.c. Read in full: it shares nothing but the generic 4-high-register push/pop prologue shape common to many owners in this compiler's output. No shared callees, field offsets, or constants. This is the same family-clustering false positive already documented on this owner's sibling (see below) -- not a genuine match, and not usable as a source-shape starting point.

This owner is the row-scanning counterpart to games/gs1/recon/en/main/0800ff54.c (Func_0800ff54, also an un-adopted measured-draft, 172 bytes). Both share the identical four-word literal pool (0x06002800, 0x02010000, 0x02020000, 0x02020004) and setup idiom: truncating-divide-by-2-then-mod-128 of a coordinate for a toroidal 128x128 source index, plus '& 30'-then-shift for a wrapped VRAM destination offset. 0800fec8 holds the source ROW fixed (from a2) and walks 16 SOURCE COLUMNS (from a1) in one call, writing a full 32-bit (2-tile) pair per iteration -- the row variant. 0800ff54 holds the source COLUMN fixed (from a1) and walks 11 source rows (from a2), writing one 16-bit tile at a time selected by an a1&1 parity bit -- the column variant, which needs the parity trick because adjacent destination rows are 64 bytes apart (not adjacent), so a paired 32-bit store isn't possible there. The two are plausibly declared in the same original source file.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to 0800ff54.json's classification/domain text and its CopyBlock helper: that draft's C labels 0x02020000 as the source 'map' cell array and 0x02010000 as the 'colors' lookup table -- backwards. Recomputing 0800ff54.s's own PC-relative ldr targets by hand (ldr r4,[pc,#80] at instruction #40, address 0x0800ffa2 -> pc-word 0x0800ffa4 -> target 0x0800ffa4+0x50 = 0x0800fff4, which is literal slot 2 = 0x02010000) shows the row+col-indexed array 0800ff54 reads from is 0x02010000 (the field cell array, matching games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/field/field_owner_123.c and games/gs1/src/map/get_cell_collision.c, both already-adopted-exact and both indexing 0x02010000 by (x + y*128)*4), and the metatile-id-indexed lookup is 0x02020000/0x02020004 -- i.e. the same role assignment established independently here for 0800fec8, both by hand-trace and by m2c against real types. This does not change 0800ff54's byte-exactness score (both literals compile to the same instruction shapes regardless of which specific address is embedded), but its prose and CopyBlock's argument naming describe the wrong array for each role and should be corrected in a future pass.

Extensive register-allocation experimentation (13 source-shape variants tried: named row/rowmod/col/colmod/destination locals in several declaration orders, do-while vs for, a helper function vs full inlining, u8* vs plain-u32 destination arithmetic, '(cell & 0xFFF) * 8' vs the shift-fusion '(cell << 20) >> 17' spelling, m2c's own flattened everything-recomputed-per-iteration shape cleaned up with casts) converged on the same wall the sibling 0800ff54 already hit and documented: the reference needs only two extra high registers across the loop (r8 and sl, holding the 0x7F/30 wrap masks, with the VRAM destination base parked in ip -- a register that never needs saving) but every source shape tried here compiles to three (r8, r9, sl -- ip never gets used for the destination base at all, forcing a third saved high register). Best result (this draft): candidate 144 bytes vs 140 reference, 64/88 differing halfwords out of 88, matched_prefix=2. Hoisting row/rowmod/destination into named locals before the loop (matching the reference's own register roles most literally) was consistently WORSE (candidate grew to 160 bytes, 78-81 differing) than recomputing them inline each iteration and only carrying col/colmod/counter across iterations, which is the shape this draft uses.

This is a global register-allocation priority difference in the approved compiler, not a local expression-shape bug -- the same conclusion 0800ff54.json's rejected_experiments reached for its own residual. No combination tried here persuaded the allocator to leave the destination base in ip the way the reference does.
